name: D-Score robustness — does a parcel ranking survive disputed weights
summary: Checks whether two parcels keep their D-Score order when stakeholders dispute the indicator weights, using the sharp bound score drift ≤ total variation of the weights × range of the indicators.

reconciliation.note: The package's Lean status in the canon catalog is 'working' (not spine-admitted); Viridis OS admitted the DOI to its bundled canon index by the owner's decision on 2026-10-31, but the canon classification must be reconciled before admission as a function.

inputs.name: reference_weights
inputs.help: The agreed (reference) indicator weights, as a list that sums to 1.

inputs.name: alternative_weights
inputs.help: The disputed (alternative) weights, same length, summing to 1.

inputs.name: parcel_a
inputs.help: Parcel A's indicator values, one per weight.

inputs.name: parcel_b
inputs.help: Parcel B's indicator values, one per weight.

hypotheses.statement: Both weight vectors are non-negative and sum to 1.
hypotheses.check: all(x >= 0 for x in reference_weights) and all(x >= 0 for x in alternative_weights)

hypotheses.statement: Weights and both parcels have the same number of indicators.
hypotheses.check: len(reference_weights) == len(alternative_weights) and len(parcel_a) == len(reference_weights) and len(parcel_b) == len(reference_weights)

expected_outputs.scope: weighted-sum arithmetic for two parcels; ecological validity of the D-Score not proven

scope: Weighted-sum arithmetic for two parcels under two weight vectors on a shared indicator set.
boundary: The D-Score's ecological validity is not proven: this does not show the indicators measure ecosystem condition, that any weighting is correct, or that a ranking should drive a decision. The result is conditional on the supplied inputs; it does not establish empirical validity, Viridis review, certification, a credit, or a registry determination.
